_comment: The bootstrap instance. It declares two directories — `skills/` and `workflows/` — because discovery reads declarations rather than walking the tree, and an undeclared directory is not this instance's graph however many files sit in it. ONE process lives here and only one: `workflows/initialize-harness.bpmn`. That is deliberate — an Initiator that has read README.md is at its start event with nowhere else to go, and one diagram cannot be confused with another. Cat-harness is composed ON TOP of this rather than being its parent, which is why nothing here may import from it.

assets.title: AGENTS.md — bootstrap
assets.description: Phase one of two. Valid with nothing installed: no skills, no knowledge graph, no MCP, no beans. The default behaviour of initialisation is to copy this file, and the last bootstrap step re-enters through the installed harness, which is what supplies phase two. No `source` because this is the origin — an absent source means authored here, which is a different fact from an upstream that cannot be reached.

assets.title: bootstrap
assets.description: The flow, with every term linked to the schema that defines it. Self-documenting on GitHub: a person landing on the directory reads the thing itself rather than a pointer to a site.

_directories_comment: ONE entry, and it is a subdirectory rather than `bootstrap/` itself. `isSkillMd` is declaration-over-location: a markdown file that does NOT declare `$schema:` is a skill. README.md and AGENTS.md declare neither, so a graph rooted at `bootstrap/` would count this instance's two DECLARED ASSETS as skill nodes — the instance has already said what those files are, and a scan would contradict its own declaration. Keeping the graph one level down means the two mechanisms cannot collide. Declared explicitly rather than relying on DEFAULT_DIRECTORIES: a declaration that exists is honoured as written, so defaults do not apply to an instance that declares anything at all.

stickies._comment: Bootstrap contributes its OWN card, which is the whole point of the contribution seam: this file cannot import cat-harness, so a code registry would be a seam bootstrap could not reach. ORDER 90 is bootstrap's own judgement that it is the least interesting card on the board — a layer can only state its own priority, it cannot see the others, and without a declared order the board would render in dependency-resolution order (deepest dependency first), putting this above the instance's own description. THEME `pale-sage` is PALETTE-ONLY: it declares no imageRole, so this sticky resolves to no backdrop at all. That is the owner's ruling — "i want the grumpy cat moved out of bootstrap and into cat harness" — made structural rather than remembered. NO GH-PAGES LINK: the owner asked for "link back to the source code + ghpaghes for boot strrap", and bootstrap HAS NO SITE. This instance's canonicalUrl is cat-harness's site, not bootstrap's. Declaring a link to a page that does not exist would be a 404 on the landing page; add one line here when the URL exists.

directories.description: The bootstrap PROCESS — `bootstrap.bpmn`, the decision tree. Declared because discovery reads declarations rather than walking the tree: until 2026-09-19 `findBpmnDirs` found this directory by WALKING from the repository root, which also walked it into folio-assistant's graph (88 references to `Process_Bootstrap` in `_kg/folio-assistant.jsonld`, measured). A separate id from `cat-harness`, because overrides match on id and `skills/` already holds that one — reusing it would replace bootstrap's skills with its workflows.
